scenes.line1: Why do some UI tests fail randomly?
scenes.say: Ever had a test pass, then fail for no reason? Let's talk about why UI tests get flaky—and how to fix them.

scenes.label: Causes
scenes.sub: Timing, unstable selectors, network delays, or bad test data.
scenes.say: Flaky tests usually fail because of timing issues, unstable selectors, network hiccups, or inconsistent data.
To fix flakiness, use better selectors, add smart waits, keep your test data steady, and isolate tests from outside systems.
If an element isn't visible yet, add an explicit wait for visibility. This makes your test more reliable.

scenes.question: Should you use nth-child in selectors?
scenes.right: No. Nth-child is fragile—use stable IDs or roles instead.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Avoid using nth-child or dynamic classes. They're fragile and break easily. Stick to stable IDs or roles.
